title: Multi-slab benchmarking: token efficiency, stability and drift detection across A10/L4/A100/H100
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: build a repeatable, statistically-sound benchmarking and load-testing harness that runs across our hardware matrix (A10, L4, A100, H100) to measure tokens/sec, p95 latency, and cost-per-token. The harness should detect regressions and drift over time, surface actionable signals to SRE/Runtime teams, and produce weekly cost-efficiency reports segmented by model family, quantization, and kernel configurations.

Motivation: existing scripts capture isolated throughput points but do not provide long-term drift detection or consistent cost normalization across GPU types. We need a 'multi-slab' harness that:
- standardizes workload profiles (seq lengths, prompt shapes, batching)
- produces reproducible token/sec and latency distributions
- stores historical baselines and computes statistical regressions
- computes cost-per-token using our internal cost model and cloud list prices

Scope: implement harness code + CI integration + nightly full-matrix runner + dashboards + alerting. Instrumentation should emit to metrics store (TimescaleDB) and push summary events to monitoring (Grafana/Alertmanager + Slack).
acceptance_criteria:
1) End-to-end harness that runs the full matrix (A10/L4/A100/H100) with configured workloads and stores metrics in TimescaleDB.
2) Produced metrics include tokens_per_sec (mean/median), latency p50/p95/p99, token distribution, sample stderr, and cost_per_token computed with the team's pricing model.
3) Regression detector runs nightly comparing current run to 30-run rolling baseline using median + MAD and a non-parametric test (Mann-Whitney) — flags if tokens/sec drops >10% or p95 increases >20% with p<0.01.
4) Grafana dashboard with per-GPU/per-model heatmap and trend panels is available and linked in ticket.
5) Alert workflow: when a regression is detected, create Linear ticket draft, send Slack alert to #runtime-bench (with run id, delta, screenshot link) and include regression diagnostics (top N diffs, kernel/quantization variants).
6) Weekly cost-per-token report auto-generated and uploaded to Drive with CSV and summary text.
7) CI: PRs touching runtime scheduler or kernel selection trigger a smoke microbench job that runs small fixed scenarios and fails PR if latency regressions exceed thresholds.
test_plan:
1) Unit tests for measurement library (correct tokens counting, latency buckets).
2) Integration test: run harness on a single GPU (A10) in CI to validate end-to-end emission to a mock Timescale instance.
3) Nightly full-matrix run in staging cluster (not production) to gather baseline.
4) Synthetic regression injection: run harness with intentional kernel slowdown to verify alerting and ticket creation.
5) Compare cost_per_token numbers against historical artifacts (ENG-9473, ENG-12840) for sanity.
6) Run statistical engine against archived runs to verify false positive rate under 30-run baseline.
notes:
Design decisions and trade-offs: 
- Use non-parametric tests because token/sec distributions are often skewed.
- Baseline = rolling window of last 30 successful full-matrix nightly runs; fallback to last 7 if 30 unavailable.
- Use median + MAD for robust central tendency and spread.
- Cost model: internal hourly GPU rate + fixed infra premium; include sensitivity analysis for spot price swings.
- For CI PR smoke tests we only run small sequence lengths and single-batch to keep cost/time low.

Open questions: 
- Do we store raw per-request traces permanently or only summaries to limit storage? Proposal: keep raw traces for 7 days and aggregated summaries retained for 1 year.
- Threshold tuning: start with tokens/sec drop of 10% and p95 increase 20%; iterate after 2 weeks.

Implementation notes: harness lives under repo infra/benchmarks/multislab. Nightly runner orchestrated by Airflow DAG bench_full_matrix_v2. Metrics emitted with tags: gpu_type, model_family, quant, seq_len, batch_size, kernel_id, run_id.
